title: Intermittent 504s under traffic spikes from leaked database connections
problem: Payment authorization requests timed out during traffic spikes.
symptoms: Intermittent HTTP 504s under heavy load; the summary identifies connection leakage after errors but supplies no latency, error-rate, or pool-utilization measurements.
root_cause: Error paths failed to release PostgreSQL connections to the bounded psycopg pool, exhausting available connections.

attempted_solutions.result: Failed to correct the connection leak; requests still depended on connections that were not returned.

successful_solution: Implemented proper connection cleanup, bounded connection waiting, and pool monitoring.
outcome: The summary reports the underlying cause was addressed and all nine repository tests passed in GitHub CI; no before/after load-test figures were supplied. Evidence: supplied repository summary; no incident commit or issue identifier was supplied. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Traffic-spike timeouts coincide with connections not being returned after failures. Compare checkout-service provider timeouts and payments-api migration blocking before applying this fix.

title: Index migration blocks authorization writes
problem: An index migration increased authorization API latency while PostgreSQL writes were blocked.
symptoms: Write blocking and API latency during an index migration; no measured duration or error rate was supplied.
root_cause: The index migration blocked database writes; increasing application capacity could not remove the database lock.

attempted_solutions.result: Failed because additional API processes still depended on the same blocked database writes.

successful_solution: Used concurrent index creation and migration safeguards documented in migration runbooks.
outcome: The summary reports the migration cause was addressed. The repository has nine passing GitHub CI tests, but no migration benchmark or safeguard details were supplied. Evidence: supplied repository summary; no incident commit or issue identifier was supplied. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Latency starts during an index migration and writes are blocked. Distinguish lock contention from leaked connections and downstream provider latency.

title: Provider-induced checkout 504s despite healthy database metrics
problem: Checkout waited too long for the downstream mock payment provider.
symptoms: Checkout 504s occurred with a slow downstream provider while database metrics remained healthy; the original provider timeout was 10 seconds.
root_cause: The downstream provider was slow and the client allowed long waits; database connection exhaustion was not the cause.

attempted_solutions.result: Did not help because the provider, rather than the database, was slow.

successful_solution: Reduced the provider timeout to 600 milliseconds, initially limited the client to one attempt, and added a circuit breaker opening after three failures. A later retry fix allows at most two provider attempts.
outcome: Timeout and breaker-recovery tests were added; all nine final checkout tests pass according to the summary. No production latency reduction was reported. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 661c873; merged PR #5; resolved issue #1. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: 504s are attributable to downstream provider calls while database metrics are healthy; compare payments-api connection leakage before reusing a timeout fix.

title: Two retry layers amplify provider failures to nine attempts
problem: A failing provider triggered excessive attempts for each checkout.
symptoms: The initial orchestration and provider-client retry layers could issue up to nine provider attempts per checkout.
root_cause: Retries at both layers multiplied attempts rather than sharing a single retry owner.

attempted_solutions.result: Made the retry storm worse by allowing more work against the failing provider.

attempted_solutions.solution: Retried in both checkout orchestration and the provider client.
attempted_solutions.result: The original implementation amplified a single checkout into as many as nine provider attempts.

successful_solution: Removed orchestration retries; made the provider client the sole retry owner with at most two attempts, jittered backoff, no retries for permanent errors, a limit of eight concurrent retries, and the same idempotency key.
outcome: The documented maximum fell from nine provider attempts to two. The final repository suite has nine passing tests; no throughput measurements were supplied. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 6cacb36; merged PR #6; resolved issue #2. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Nested retries amplify downstream outages. Relevant to payments-api callers, but retry ownership must be coordinated across layers.

title: Repeated checkout requests return different order IDs
problem: Clients retrying a checkout could receive a newly generated order instead of the original result.
symptoms: The initial implementation generated a fresh order ID on every request; duplicate-request handling needed to survive reopening the database.
root_cause: Successful normalized requests and responses were not durably associated with their idempotency keys.

attempted_solutions.solution: Generated a fresh order ID for every incoming request.
attempted_solutions.result: This initial implementation did not replay the original order on retries; the summary does not describe a separate failed remediation.

successful_solution: Required an idempotency key, stored normalized requests and successful responses in SQLite, replayed the original result for identical retries, returned 409 for conflicting payloads, and protected concurrent requests within one process.
outcome: Added concurrent-retry and database-reopen replay tests; the final nine tests pass. Multi-replica coordination and real-provider reconciliation remain outside scope. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 6ead437; merged PR #7; resolved issue #3. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: A retried operation must return its original successful response and reject key reuse with different payloads. The supplied implementation applies only within a single process.

title: Misnamed configuration silently routes staging calls to localhost
problem: A misnamed environment variable allowed checkout to use an unintended localhost downstream address in staging.
symptoms: The staging scenario involved silent localhost fallback; exact HTTP errors were not supplied.
root_cause: Startup accepted missing or incorrect downstream configuration instead of failing before serving requests.

attempted_solutions.solution: Allowed a localhost default when downstream configuration was missing.
attempted_solutions.result: The initial behavior hid the misnamed environment variable and selected the wrong destination; no separate failed remediation was described.

successful_solution: Validated required downstream URLs and timeout settings at startup and supplied .env.example.
outcome: Configuration tests were added and all nine final tests pass; the summary also notes database-handle cleanup in this commit. No deployment success-rate measurement was supplied. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 0971a88; merged PR #8; resolved issue #4. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Service-to-service failures follow deployment configuration changes, especially when a development default masks a missing setting. Relevant to payments-api and fleetapi startup validation.

title: Vehicle search SQL injection found during security review
problem: Vehicle search and filtering constructed SQL using request values.
symptoms: A security review found an injection vulnerability before any exploitation was reported.
root_cause: Search SQL was assembled through string concatenation.

attempted_solutions.solution: Built search/filter SQL through string concatenation in commit bc5822f.
attempted_solutions.result: The initial implementation introduced SQL injection; no separate failed fix was documented in the summary.

outcome: The fix and postmortem are recorded in commit edf6f25; regression coverage for SQL injection was later added in commit 7df5bc2. No exploitation was reported. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit edf6f25. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Request values enter SQL queries. Applicable to SQLite in checkout-service and PostgreSQL in payments-api, using each driver’s parameter syntax.

title: Hardcoded JWT secret and non-expiring tokens require auth hardening
problem: JWT authentication shipped with an embedded signing secret and tokens without expiration.
symptoms: The synthetic leaked-secret incident identified the hardcoded secret and unlimited token lifetime; no exploitation or affected-token count was supplied.
root_cause: The initial authentication implementation embedded the signing secret and omitted token expiry.

attempted_solutions.solution: Used a hardcoded secret and tokens that never expired in commit 7c76b77.
attempted_solutions.result: This initial design left the signing secret exposed in source and tokens valid indefinitely; no separate failed remediation was described.

successful_solution: Moved the signing secret into a required environment variable, rotated it, and set token expiration to eight hours.
outcome: The fix and postmortem are recorded in commit 06d3b45. The summary does not report auth-specific test results or token revocation measurements. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 06d3b45. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: A service uses embedded signing credentials or unbounded token lifetimes; required startup configuration also relates to checkout-service’s configuration incident.

title: Pagination skips the first page of results
problem: List endpoint pagination omitted the first page after pagination was introduced.
symptoms: A pilot customer reported skipped page-one results.
root_cause: The SQL offset calculation had an off-by-one error for one-based page numbers.

attempted_solutions.solution: Used the original pagination offset calculation in commit 828fc4c.
attempted_solutions.result: It skipped page one; the exact original expression and a separate attempted fix were not supplied.

outcome: Commit ac8d95b fixes the calculation; pagination regression coverage was later added in commit 7df5bc2. No affected-row count was supplied. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit ac8d95b. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: An API exposes one-based page numbers but its storage query uses zero-based offsets.

title: Concurrent fuel logs lose odometer increments
problem: Fuel logging updated vehicle odometers through separate read and write operations.
symptoms: Concurrent updates produced a lost-update race; no reproduction counts were supplied.
root_cause: Two operations could read the same previous odometer value and overwrite each other’s increments.

attempted_solutions.solution: Read the odometer, computed a new value, and wrote it back in commit d4f7696.
attempted_solutions.result: The initial read-modify-write approach was not atomic and allowed lost updates; no separate failed remediation was documented.

successful_solution: Used a single atomic UPDATE with SET odometer = odometer + ? instead of application-side read-modify-write.
outcome: Commit 79ed109 records the fix and postmortem; race-condition regression coverage was added in commit 7df5bc2. The summary says the lost-update race was closed. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 79ed109. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Concurrent requests increment a shared database value. This is distinct from duplicate operation replay in checkout-service; atomic increments alone do not provide idempotency.

title: Floating-point trip billing fails finance reconciliation
problem: Trip cost calculations and monthly reports stored and summed costs as floating-point values.
symptoms: Finance reconciliation caught monetary discrepancies; the summary supplies no discrepancy amounts.
root_cause: Floating-point storage and summation introduced rounding inaccuracies in monetary calculations.

attempted_solutions.solution: Stored and summed costs as floats in commit 52d63a6.
attempted_solutions.result: The initial representation produced reconciliation discrepancies; no separate failed remediation was documented.

successful_solution: Migrated monetary calculations and storage to integer cents throughout.
outcome: Commit fa13eec records the fix and postmortem. No reconciliation totals or migration test results were supplied. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit fa13eec. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Exact monetary accumulation is required. Relevant to checkout-service and payments-api amount handling, with currency-specific minor-unit rules considered separately.

title: N+1 driver queries cause fleet dashboard timeouts
problem: The vehicle trips endpoint became too slow for the largest pilot customer after adding driver details.
symptoms: Dashboard timeouts occurred for the largest pilot; GET /vehicles/:id/trips issued one driver query per trip.
root_cause: Per-trip driver lookups caused an N+1 query pattern as trip counts grew.

attempted_solutions.solution: Fetched driver details separately for every trip in commit 0fc2352.
attempted_solutions.result: The initial approach scaled query count with trip count and caused dashboard timeouts; no separate failed fix was described.

successful_solution: Replaced per-trip lookups with a single LEFT JOIN query.
outcome: Commit 2afd3e1 records the fix and postmortem and is described as fixing the dashboard timeouts. No latency or query-count benchmark was supplied beyond the single-query design. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 2afd3e1. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Timeouts grow with the number of related records and queries repeat per result. Compare payments-api connection leaks and checkout-service provider latency rather than applying a generic timeout increase.

title: Negative mileage and fuel values corrupt analytics
problem: A buggy upstream integration submitted invalid mileage and fuel values.
symptoms: The analytics dashboard was corrupted by negative input values; no number of affected records was supplied.
root_cause: The API lacked validation rejecting negative mileage and fuel values.

attempted_solutions.solution: Accepted upstream mileage and fuel values without the missing validation.
attempted_solutions.result: The initial behavior allowed invalid data to reach analytics; no separate failed remediation was documented.

successful_solution: Added validation middleware rejecting negative mileage and fuel values.
outcome: Commit b2b65a7 records the fix and postmortem; validation regression coverage was added in commit 7df5bc2. The summary does not establish that historical invalid records were repaired. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit b2b65a7. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Upstream integrations can submit syntactically valid but domain-invalid numbers. Related to amount validation in checkout-service and payments-api.

title: Local-time timestamp parsing produces DST duration errors
problem: The trip-end response added duration_minutes but interpreted timestamps in local time.
symptoms: Trip durations were incorrect around daylight-saving transitions; no example timestamp pair was supplied.
root_cause: Timestamp parsing depended on local-time interpretation rather than explicit UTC.

attempted_solutions.solution: Parsed trip timestamps as local time in commit 7e64edf.
attempted_solutions.result: The original duration calculation was vulnerable to DST-related errors; no separate failed remediation was documented.

successful_solution: Parsed timestamps explicitly as UTC for duration calculations.
outcome: Commit 1afea0c is described as avoiding DST-related duration errors. No timezone regression test results were supplied. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 1afea0c. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Elapsed durations are calculated from timestamps whose interpretation must remain stable across host timezones and daylight-saving changes.

title: Invalid driver ID crashes trip start with raw SQL error
problem: Trip start failed without a controlled validation response when driver_id was invalid.
symptoms: The defect was found while writing tests; the previous behavior crashed with a raw SQL error.
root_cause: The trip-start path did not validate driver_id before using it in the database operation.

attempted_solutions.solution: Passed driver_id into the trip-start operation without validation.
attempted_solutions.result: The initial behavior exposed a raw SQL failure; no separate failed remediation was documented.

successful_solution: Validated driver_id on trip start before the database operation.
outcome: Commit e2c8018 fixes the defect identified during test development. The summary does not specify the resulting status code or full validation rules. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit e2c8018. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: A reference supplied by a caller can fail database constraints and escape as an uncontrolled error. Relevant to any API accepting related-entity IDs.

title: ADR: SQLite accepted for a single-instance MVP
problem: The fleet backend needed a storage choice for an MVP with vehicles, drivers, trips, maintenance, and users.
symptoms: No incident is documented for this decision; the summary explicitly identifies a single-instance tradeoff.
root_cause: Architectural constraint: the fixture selected SQLite for its MVP and accepted a single-instance deployment boundary.

attempted_solutions.solution: Implemented the core schema with SQLite and better-sqlite3 in commit 082c8f3.
attempted_solutions.result: Adopted for the MVP with the single-instance tradeoff accepted; no failed alternative is documented.

successful_solution: Recorded the SQLite MVP decision and accepted single-instance limitation in ADR 0001. This is an accepted design, not a resolved scaling incident.
outcome: Commit 3e830b6 records ADR 0001. No multi-instance readiness or performance outcome is claimed. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit 3e830b6. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Selecting storage for a small single-instance service; relevant to checkout-service’s SQLite replay store, whose multi-replica coordination is also outside scope.

title: ADR: Stateless JWT authentication decision
problem: The fleet backend needed an authentication design and a recorded rationale.
symptoms: No separate operational incident is documented in this ADR summary. The original JWT implementation later required secret and expiry fixes.
root_cause: Architectural decision: use stateless JWT authentication; the detailed rationale and evaluated alternatives were not included in the supplied summary.

attempted_solutions.result: The approach was adopted, but its initial hardcoded secret and non-expiring tokens required the separate fix in commit 06d3b45; no rejected alternative is documented.

successful_solution: Recorded the stateless JWT rationale in ADR 0002. Implementation hardening is captured in the separate leaked-secret precedent.
outcome: Commit be9cfc4 records ADR 0002. This is a design record, not evidence that the original authentication implementation was secure. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit be9cfc4. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: Reviewing the rationale for stateless authentication while separately checking credential management and token-expiration behavior.

title: ADR: In-memory per-IP rate limiting does not coordinate across instances
problem: The fleet API introduced a per-IP limiter with process-local state.
symptoms: No rate-limit outage is documented; ADR 0003 explicitly accepts that the limiter does not work across multiple instances.
root_cause: Each process keeps its own in-memory limiter state, so the implementation does not coordinate limits between instances.

attempted_solutions.solution: Implemented an in-memory per-IP limiter in commit 0a195b2.
attempted_solutions.result: Accepted for the fixture’s deployment boundary, but ineffective as a shared multi-instance limit; no failed distributed implementation is documented.

successful_solution: Documented the limitation in ADR 0003 rather than implementing distributed coordination. No multi-instance fix is claimed.
outcome: Commit a0b7d2e records the accepted limitation. The summary provides no quota values, load tests, or shared-store implementation. Evidence: supplied repository summary identifies commit a0b7d2e. Incident history is synthetic; source code and test outputs were not independently inspected.
applicable_when: A process-local control is considered for replicated deployment. Relevant to checkout-service’s single-process concurrency protection, though rate limiting and idempotency enforce different guarantees.
